speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the number of CPF members aged 65 to 67 years old who are still in employment; and (b) whether the Government is considering increasing the age limit for the Dependants' Protection Scheme from the current 65 years old.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: asked the Minister for Manpower for each year in the past three years, what is the number of CPF members below the age of 65 whose Dependants' Protection Scheme coverage has lapsed due to non-payment of premium.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We regularly review the DPS to ensure that it remains relevant to members.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In taking this decision, we sought to strike a balance between providing insurance protection for members’ dependants for a longer period, while at the same time, ensuring the adequacy of members' retirement savings.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Raising the maximum coverage age beyond 65 would result in higher premiums due to higher mortality rates after age 65 and consequentially, would reduce members' savings for retirement.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: All members will receive notifications via both SMS and mail if their CPF balances are insufficient and they can opt to pay their DPS premiums in cash.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Those who wish to re-join the scheme can subsequently still apply to Great Eastern Life, which is the current administrator of DPS to do so.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I have three supplementary questions to my first Parliamentary Question and one supplementary question to my second Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: On coverage for seniors above 65, my supplementary questions would be – I understand that there are implications in terms of premium cost, but more seniors are remaining in the workforce beyond 65.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In fact, our own Re-employment Age has moved to 67.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And they are supporting dependants, both children as well as seniors, with our increased life expectancy.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: So, would the Minister consider the current age limit to remain appropriate and fit-for-purpose, given the current realities?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Two, could the Minister share what actuarial studies have been done on the feasibility of extending DPS coverage to align with the current Re-employment Age and what the implications might there be for premiums?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: How much of an increase are we talking about?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And thirdly, if a broad-based approach is too costly, could the Minister consider more targeted approaches or optional DPS extension, perhaps at a higher premium?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Because I think of the cost of not having coverage, if something bad happens and DPS is a great scheme.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: It would be great for those who are still in employment to benefit from it.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: On the Parliamentary Question on non-payment, I appreciate the data that there is only 0.2%, which is quite comforting.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Does the Minister have insights on the reason for non-payment?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Is it mostly due to financial difficulties or is it lack of awareness?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The Minister mentioned that members could apply, so, I am glad to know that there are grace periods.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Could the Minister also consider additional safeguards, in terms of premium assistance and more flexible reinstatement arrangements to support people who really need it?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think there are a total of six supplementary questions; three for each one of the Parliamentary Questions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I will try to address all of them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have said, we constantly review these.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But with the very fact that we are also rapidly ageing and the age of the workforce is also getting there, if we have a sizeable pool, looking at how that pooling of that premium can be spread across, I think extending coverage is certainly something that we are open to considering.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have not stopped reviewing this framework because we want to try to provide for the coverage for as long as possible.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But we always have to balance between sustainability, affordability and also, ensuring that there is a sufficient sum left behind for the members to tap on when they are finally eligible for that payout, at age of 65 or 70, depending on how they choose.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: With regard to the Member's point on non-payment, for those members whose DPS coverage has lapsed, about 75% of them are aged above 55 years old.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Many of them are no longer working, or they were self-employed persons before.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, this has to be taken against the broader numbers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, that number, that 75%, is of that 16% that we are really talking about.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There are obviously different types of assistance schemes that are available.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Many of these members can also reach out to some of the social agencies to see what kind of help can be rolled out to them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: What we are trying to do is to ensure that we can cover as broad-based a scheme as possible for all members if possible, but it would not be possible to cover every single one of them.
